target: 100% archival completion of the selected original i-mode route, spoiler-free

areas.name: Archived i-mode Setup
areas.location_cue: The Japanese handset boot, Capcom Park login, account synchronization, and companion clock.
areas.note: Server dependence makes preservation the first completion requirement.

items.label: Use the Original DoCoMo i-mode Build

levels.1: The game depended on a Japanese carrier service and specific phones.
levels.2: Use a preserved 503i-series handset with an authenticated historical service state.
levels.3: Preserve the handset, application storage, firmware, carrier identifiers, account state, and server responses before launching. The original game was network-dependent rather than a self-contained i-application; no current server or verified emulator replacement is documented.

levels.1: A surviving session may depend on a temporary reconstructed endpoint.
levels.2: Record boot, login, synchronization, menus, maps, combat, mail, and results.
levels.3: Capture continuously from handset boot through authentication and every server request. Export packet logs where lawful, photograph each Japanese response, and keep two copies of the application and session data before testing any destructive or irreversible command.

levels.1: A linked clock displayed recovery and network information outside play.
levels.2: Open the corresponding clock and record health, recovery time, and mail indicators.
levels.3: With the same preserved account active, open the companion clock while disconnected from the main game. Capture current HP, time remaining until recovery, and network-mail state, then compare them after one verified battle without altering the device clock.

save_backup.title: Clone the account and handset first
save_backup.why: Testing can alter the only surviving server-linked state.

areas.name: Team, Growth, and Inventory Systems
areas.location_cue: The team formation, statistics, city-node, battle, event, inventory, and synthesis menus.
areas.note: Record each server-backed mechanic before pursuing undocumented caps.

levels.1: The opening offers three candidates with different strengths.
levels.2: Create separate archival profiles and select every available initial candidate.
levels.3: From a clean account state, record the complete initial candidate screen, choose one candidate, capture starting stats and equipment, then repeat on cloned profiles for the other two. Do not assume later recruitability replaces the opening choice.

levels.1: Recruited specialists alter attack, discovery, and recovery performance.
levels.2: Add available allies, then test every formation position and role.
levels.3: After each recruit joins, record their base statistics and special ability, place them in every selectable position, and compare team Attack, Discovery, and Recovery totals. Preserve a pre-change profile before dismissing or replacing anyone.

levels.1: Combat and event resolution improve different team capabilities.
levels.2: Train Attack, Discovery, and Recovery through observed battles and events.
levels.3: Record the three values before an action, complete one battle or event, synchronize, and record the change. Repeat with formations specializing in each stat until the surviving build stops granting growth; treat that observed ceiling as provisional until reproduced.

levels.1: Familiar supplies return inside a menu-driven inventory.
levels.2: Acquire every item displayed by the surviving server state.
levels.3: Search each available city node and event, record the item name and quantity before pickup, then verify it in the inventory. Use a cloned profile to test consumption, equipment, trading, or loss without damaging the archive account.

levels.1: Some inventory objects can be synthesized into stronger equipment.
levels.2: Open the combination menu and test only displayed compatible pairs.
levels.3: Record every selectable ingredient pair, clone the profile, combine it, and capture the resulting name and statistics. Restore after failed or consumptive tests; do not infer recipes that the surviving interface never offers.

levels.1: Teams in the same area can cooperate against a shared event.
levels.2: Meet another preserved team in one city node and choose cooperation.
levels.3: Using two lawful preserved accounts, place both teams in the same available area, initiate the joint-front command, exchange the displayed information, complete one cooperative enemy or event resolution, and capture rewards for both accounts.

levels.1: The network offered optional team-versus-team simulation.
levels.2: Meet another team and initiate the mock-battle option.
levels.3: Back up both profiles, record formations and stats, issue the mock-battle request, accept it on the second account, and capture every round and result field. Restore afterward if defeat changes resources or standing.

save_backup.title: Back up before formation or synthesis changes
save_backup.why: Recruits and ingredients may not be recoverable on a retired service.
